Stellar Blade delivers an exhilarating experience that blends fast, fluid combat with rich exploration. Every fight feels impactful and I really love the focus on perfectly timed parries and away from the dodge style souls-likes. The environments are breathtaking, encouraging you to explore every corner for hidden lore and upgrades, while the soundtrack elevates every moment—clearly inspired by the NieR series, and it absolutely nails that emotional resonance. I find myself taking in the world and just listening to the 10/10 Soundtrack the game has to offer even way before the game was released on PC. 

I was really excited to play this one. I look forward to Stellar Blade 2 in the future

One line sums up the journey best: “May your memories live on forever.” This game isn’t just action—it’s an unforgettable experience.

Loads of style and good combat, though the platforming at times can feel off, it's not bad just not great. I really enjoy the parry-punish style combat which made for a wicked hard boss battle near the end requiring great timing. There's lots of skins to find along the way, mostly by being curious and exploring, looking for secret areas. It uses the Dark Souls rest/enemy respawn system. I find it plays more like Jedi Survivor than Dark Souls though, just overall. Great graphics, ultrawide and HDR support. There's a new game + and new game ++ to find even more variations of the skins though these are mostly colour variants of ones you have already if you found them the first time through. There's some new enhancements to skills and can upgrade your health and such further in NG+. Would recommend if the things I mentioned sound good to you. I personally really enjoyed my time with it.

Writing this on low playtime because I played through this game on PS5 already.

Look, I’m not gonna goon out or wax poetic about the main character’s aesthetics—everything that could be said about her has already been said. If you're allergic to good-lookin' ladies, maybe steer clear. I dunno. That’s your call.

What I *really* want to stress is that this has to be one of the best modern PC ports out there and an absolute tour de force in Unreal Engine optimization. The demo instantly impressed me with how well it ran, and the full game delivers exactly the same experience. So far, performance and stability have been flawless (Update: 8 hours in, I still haven't had a single issue). With i7-13700k and RTX4080 I can run this at the absolute highest settings at super stable 130+fps at 1440p and this is without any DLSS or Frame Generation. Those settings are still available if you need them and should carry you pretty well even on older hardware.

I genuinely believe this level of optimization should be the standard for PC releases. Huge props to Shift Up for keeping the art alive.

Beyond that, the game just freakin’ rules. It's very NieR-coded—sometimes maybe borrowing a bit too much from it—but even if it never quite hits those same emotional highs, it's still a great time. The inspired world, fantastic visuals, rewarding combat, and killer soundtrack more than make up for it.

Really great 30 (ish) hour game when played pretty casually (eg. normal difficulty, one playthrough, doing about half of the side quests). The combat feels extremely fluid and fun. The parrying and perfect dodges feel satisfying. And the world and aesthetic/vibe are pretty solid. It is admittedly a bit of a Nier rip off at times, but I prefer to see it as a homage/love letter.

On that note, the story is decent and the characters are pretty likeable. There's nothing mind blowing here, especially if you have played Nier: Automata (which executes its story and emotional aspects far better). However, it's definitely engaging enough, and when paired with the consistently smooth and fun gameplay, the game is a delight to play.

Eve herself obviously has drawn a lot of... attention. But, all of that aside she's a fun protagonist to play as and there's a fair amount of tasteful/immersive cosmetics offered in the game that aren't distracting and over the top for those (like myself) who prefer that generally.

Any Nier fan, souls-like fan or anyone who just enjoy good action games will have a great time here. This game is what it says on the tin and it executes its main selling points perfectly well.

So, overall I'd give it a very respectable 8.5/10.

Stellar Blade is a game if you're looking for an action RPG with male gaze eye candy and satisfying skill spamming, combo button mashing gameplay.
If you are looking for stellar puzzle, story or experience design however, you'll find it lacking by the end of the game.

Pros:
The main highlight of this game is its combat. While it might not be quite as tight as the genre’s best, pulling off parries, dodges, and combos still feels immensely satisfying—especially as executing them builds momentum against enemies. To keep things interesting, enemy variety is generous and offers a solid challenge.

Character customization is amazing as well, with many costume to find with accessories and hairstyles making doing side quest worth while.

Cons:
While the game is visually stunning, the narrative lacks depth and substance. The level design suffers from repetitive environmental themes—mostly endless sand, deserts, and underground tunnels—with few memorable set pieces to break up the monotony. The story manages to keep you hooked through suspense, but ultimately unravels at the end into a string of predictable clichés.

All in all, its a very high quality game that is well executed enough to feel good to play and progress but lacks the final depth and quality to call it a true classic or "Game of the Year" material.

Fast combat, gorgeous visuals, amazing soundtrack — Stellar Blade actually lives up to the hype.
9.5/10 — Stylish, smooth, and insanely fun.

Fun Combat, Forgettable Story

Stellar Blade is all about the combat, and it absolutely nails it. If you love fast-paced, stylish action games that reward skill, you'll feel right at home. Parrying and dodging through enemy combos feels incredibly satisfying, and the boss fights are a real highlight. The game also looks and sounds fantastic.

The downside is that the story and characters are pretty generic. I found myself skipping through dialogue to get back to the action. The side quests are also mostly simple fetch quests that can feel like a chore.

Recommended?

Yes, absolutely—if you're here for the gameplay. If you're looking for a deep story, you might be disappointed. But if you want a slick, challenging, and beautiful action game to sink your teeth into, Stellar Blade is a fantastic choice.
